**Beginner Tier** (24 lessons) - How a market works, what it costs, what risk is

• What a fill is, and the five numbers a candle keeps out of its interval

kb.rsi:
**Oscillators and RSI:**

**Main Lesson:** [Lesson 51: Oscillators Under Regime](/education/curriculum/intermediate/51-oscillators-under-regime.html)

**Key Concepts:**
• An oscillator is a function of prices you already have, so it adds no information
• The same reading means different things in a trend and in a range
• What matters is what the oscillator discards, and how long it takes to discard it
• A threshold is a setting, not a measurement, and it has to be stated

**Related:** [Lesson 48: What an Indicator Is](/education/curriculum/intermediate/48-what-an-indicator-is.html), [Lesson 36: Markets Have Modes](/education/curriculum/intermediate/36-markets-have-modes.html)

**Common mistake:** Reading an extreme as a signal without first stating the regime, and without ever measuring how often the reading was right
kb.spread:
**The Spread:**

**Main Lesson:** [Lesson 4: The Spread Is the Price of Immediacy](/education/curriculum/beginner/04-the-spread.html)

**Key Concepts:**
• The spread is what immediacy costs, not a fee somebody charges you
• It is one of four charges, and lesson 10 prices all four on one trade
• Ranked against what an instrument moves in a day, the cost runs from a fifth of one per cent to 52 per cent
• Posting instead of crossing earns the spread, and lesson 58 prices what that gives away

**Related:** [Lesson 10: Every Trade Starts Negative](/education/curriculum/beginner/10-every-trade-starts-negative.html), [Lesson 53: What the Spread Is Paying For](/education/curriculum/advanced/53-market-makers-business.html)

**Where the numbers are:** Lesson 12 ranks instruments by cost as a share of daily movement
kb.automation:
**Automation and Execution:**

**Main Lesson:** [Lesson 69: The Delay You Remove](/education/curriculum/advanced/69-automation.html)

**Key Concepts:**
• Automation removes a delay; the question is what that delay was costing
• Slippage and fees belong in the backtest, because they are in the result
• A hard daily-loss limit binds before any other limit you set
• The pace you actually trade at is measurable, and it is slower than most plans assume

**Related:** [Lesson 75: Which Limit Binds First](/education/curriculum/professional/75-institutional-risk-controls.html), [Lesson 76: The Pace You Actually Trade At](/education/curriculum/professional/76-trading-day.html)

**Rule:** Deploy nothing whose failure you have not priced
kb.chatbot:
**About This Chatbot:**

I'm a pattern-matching assistant (no AI API needed!) built to help you navigate the 100 lessons.

**I can help with:**
• Lesson recommendations ("What should I learn first?")
• Concept explanations ("Explain RSI regime interpretation")
• Finding lessons ("Lessons about spread costs")
• Progress tracking ("How do I track progress?")

**What I can't do:**
• Trade recommendations
• Real-time market analysis
• Account-specific advice
• Execute trades

**How I work:**
• Pattern matching (instant responses)
• Knowledge base from all 100 lessons
• No data sent to external APIs
• Conversation history saved locally

**Pro tip:** Try asking full questions like "How does bid-ask spread work as a leading indicator?" for best results!

kb.lessons:
**About Our Lessons:**

**Structure:** every lesson has the same seven parts, in this order:
• The claim - what the lesson finds, in its first 200 words, with a figure
• Prerequisites - what it spends, and which lesson measured it
• Development - the argument, built rather than asserted
• Worked example - one, with every number recomputable from the page
• Bounds - where the finding stops being true
• Problems - what to go and measure on your own data
• Sources - what the lesson leans on, and how

**Length:** 1,400 to 5,000 words. Length is an output, never a target.

**Style:** every figure on the page is derived on the page. No composite
trader, no invented track record, no P&L story. If a number is quoted from
an earlier lesson, that lesson printed it.

**Total:** 100 lessons across 4 tiers, in 14 modules

**What makes them different:**
✅ Every claim is falsifiable, and says what would disprove it
✅ Every figure is recomputed, not repeated
✅ Each lesson ends by promising what the next one finds, with its number
✅ The bounds are as long as the argument
✅ Available in 11 languages besides English

📚 [Browse All Lessons](/)

kb.professional:
**Professional Tier:**

30 lessons (slots 71-100) on carrying more than one position, the arithmetic of doing this for a living, four specialisms, and the five lessons that turn the measurements round and point them at the trader.

**What the course measures:**
• Two rules on one instrument carry 1.03 independent bets rather than two, and the total tops out at 1.06
• A wage requires 11.40 years of that wage in capital, with the verdict on the edge 10.07 years away
• The four habits run together leave 4.44 a share where adding their costs separately predicts 1.74
• A round trip of 0.1230 takes 79.7 per cent of a tenth-of-an-R edge, moving a verdict from 785 trades to 18,952

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 71: How Many Bets You Are Carrying](/education/curriculum/professional/71-positions-are-one-position.html)
• [Lesson 79: Paying Yourself Before You Know](/education/curriculum/professional/79-career-paths.html)
• [Lesson 90: The Four Habits Together](/education/curriculum/professional/90-the-four-habits-together.html)
• [Lesson 100: The Business on One Page](/education/curriculum/professional/100-the-business-on-one-page.html)

**Duration:** 7-12 min per lesson
**Best for:** anyone who can already price a round trip and wants to know what a business built on one supports
kb.cost:
**What Trading Costs:**

Four charges are taken whether the trade works or not: the spread, the commission, the slippage and the financing. Module 2 prices all four, and every later lesson subtracts them.

**What the course measures:**
• Every position opens at a loss, and financing keeps deepening it for as long as you hold
• The same $30,000 order costs $0.30 in one instrument and $80.00 in another at the same instant
• A round trip runs from 0.2 basis points on an index ETF to 467 on a micro-cap
• A simulator sets all of it to zero: a strategy reporting +$1,000 over a hundred trades nets −$700

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 10: Every Trade Starts Negative](/education/curriculum/beginner/10-every-trade-starts-negative.html)
• [Lesson 11: Slippage and Impact at Retail Size](/education/curriculum/beginner/11-slippage-and-impact.html)
• [Lesson 12: What Should You Actually Trade](/education/curriculum/beginner/12-what-should-you-trade.html)
• [Lesson 16: Sim Against Live](/education/curriculum/beginner/16-sim-against-live.html)

**Where the arithmetic is:** lesson 12 ranks instruments by cost as a share of what they move in a day.
kb.risk:
**Risk, Sizing and Ruin:**

How much to put on, where the stop belongs, and the chance a losing run ends the account. All three are computed rather than felt.

**What the course measures:**
• One winner at +2R and two losers at −1R come to nothing in R and still cost the account money
• Ruin follows from three numbers you already have: the edge, the fraction risked, and how far you may fall
• Sizing up to recover at 5 per cent a trade returns you to the high in nine careers out of a hundred
• A genuine tenth-of-an-R edge spends its 156-trade run inside a median worst drawdown of 8.82R

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 20: Position Sizing](/education/curriculum/beginner/20-position-sizing.html)
• [Lesson 21: Where the Stop Goes](/education/curriculum/beginner/21-where-the-stop-goes.html)
• [Lesson 22: Risk of Ruin](/education/curriculum/beginner/22-risk-of-ruin.html)
• [Lesson 67: The Drawdown You Should Expect](/education/curriculum/advanced/67-is-the-edge-gone.html)

**Start at:** lesson 20, which is where every later figure in R comes from.
kb.expectancy:
**Expectancy and Sample Size:**

An edge is a number, not a feeling about a chart, and the number arrives with an interval around it that most records are far too short to close.

**What the course measures:**
• E = p·b − (1−p), in units of what you risk
• Fifty trades cannot tell a method making 0.35R a trade apart from one with no edge at all
• An edge of a tenth of an R needs 785 trades gross, and 18,952 once the round trip is subtracted
• What a real edge feels like from inside is mostly like nothing

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 17: Expectancy](/education/curriculum/beginner/17-expectancy.html)
• [Lesson 18: What an Edge Feels Like](/education/curriculum/beginner/18-what-an-edge-feels-like.html)
• [Lesson 19: How Long Until You Know](/education/curriculum/beginner/19-how-long-until-you-know.html)
• [Lesson 98: The Number That Says Scale](/education/curriculum/professional/98-the-number-that-says-scale.html)

**The habit:** work out your own sample size before you quote a win rate.
kb.orderbook:
**The Order Book and Liquidity:**

What is resting, where it rests, and how little of it the quote actually describes.

**What the course measures:**
• An ordinary book rests 7,300 shares behind a quote that describes 900 of them
• Resting size costs nothing to place and nothing to withdraw, so a wall is worth what its hit rate is worth
• Orders pile at levels you can name in advance, and the piling needs no coordination
• A stop is invisible until it fires, so a pool is certain future flow nobody can observe

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 2: The Order Book](/education/curriculum/beginner/02-the-order-book.html)
• [Lesson 25: Where Liquidity Rests](/education/curriculum/intermediate/25-where-liquidity-rests.html)
• [Lesson 26: The Order Book Is Theater](/education/curriculum/intermediate/26-order-book-is-theater.html)
• [Lesson 27: The Liquidity Lie](/education/curriculum/intermediate/27-the-liquidity-lie.html)

**The correction:** lesson 27 finds intent cannot be identified from price, whatever the pattern is called.
kb.orderflow:
**Order Flow, Delta and the Tape:**

What the tape reports and what your software infers. Three of the four facts beside a print are recorded; the fourth, the side, is a guess with a known error rate.

**What the course measures:**
• The aggressor-side inference is right about four times in five
• One misclassified print of 900 shares swings a minute from plus 600 to minus 1,200
• A bar reported at plus 15 per cent delta bounds the buy share only between 50.0 and 62.5 per cent
• Two bars can share every quantity a candle records and still carry deltas of +2,820 and −1,680

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 7: Time and Sales](/education/curriculum/beginner/07-time-and-sales.html)
• [Lesson 8: Volume and Delta](/education/curriculum/beginner/08-volume-and-delta.html)
• [Lesson 28: Absorption and Exhaustion](/education/curriculum/intermediate/28-absorption-and-exhaustion.html)
• [Lesson 29: Volume at Price](/education/curriculum/intermediate/29-volume-at-price.html)

**Read next:** lesson 29 separates the count that needs no inference from the number everyone quotes.
kb.sweep:
**Sweeps and Stop Hunts:**

Price trading past a level and coming back. Whether one happened at all is decided by three settings rather than by the market.

**What the course measures:**
• Ordinary values of the three settings find 4 sweeps on the same sixty bars, or 15, or 46
• A cascade through resting stops needs no author
• The same technique is worth sixty-two thousand dollars to one participant and twenty-five to another
• The conduct actually proved in court runs at institutional size against other machines

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 27: The Liquidity Lie](/education/curriculum/intermediate/27-the-liquidity-lie.html)
• [Lesson 35: Sweeps, Beyond the First](/education/curriculum/intermediate/35-sweeps-beyond-the-first.html)
• [Lesson 61: The Number You Cannot Look Up](/education/curriculum/advanced/61-thinking-adversarially.html)

**The honest version:** count the levels your own swing rule grants itself before you count the sweeps.
kb.structure:
**Market Structure:**

The sequence of swing highs and lows a series is read as. It is not in the prices; it is produced by applying a swing definition to them, and that definition is a setting nobody quotes.

**What the course measures:**
• On the same twenty bars, ordinary settings give eight structure events, or two, or none
• Two ordinary settings disagree about who is in control on four bars in twelve
• A break of structure predicts something you can count, which is why it beats named chart patterns
• Order blocks and displacement share the same undeclared setting

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 32: Market Structure](/education/curriculum/intermediate/32-market-structure.html)
• [Lesson 33: Order Blocks and Displacement](/education/curriculum/intermediate/33-order-blocks-and-displacement.html)
• [Lesson 40: Multi-Day Structure](/education/curriculum/intermediate/40-multi-day-structure.html)

**Before you use it:** write your swing definition down, then count.
kb.divergence:
**Divergence:**

Price disagreeing with a number computed from price. Because the indicator is a function of the same prices, a divergence is an arithmetic consequence of the path rather than an independent witness to it.

**What the course measures:**
• Two settings decide whether one exists at all: a swing rule and an oscillator period
• Before either looks at an indicator, the swing rule alone decides whether there are 33 places to look or 5
• The indicator cannot add information, because it was computed from the prices

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 34: Divergence](/education/curriculum/intermediate/34-divergence.html)
• [Lesson 48: What an Indicator Is](/education/curriculum/intermediate/48-what-an-indicator-is.html)

**Worksheet:** the divergence count sheet on the resources page runs this on your own series.
kb.regime:
**Regime, Context and Timeframe:**

Which of two behaviours a stretch of series is in, measured rather than named, and what a timeframe actually is once you notice it has two settings.

**What the course measures:**
• The efficiency ratio separates a sideways stretch from a rally completely, and carries a window
• Change the window from ten closes to thirty and the two readings disagree on 22 of 30 bars
• Regroup sixty bars four at a time and the swing count falls from 15 to 2 while the high and low do not move
• Move only the starting bar and the same ratio runs from 0.104 to 0.249 on identical tape

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 36: Markets Have Modes](/education/curriculum/intermediate/36-markets-have-modes.html)
• [Lesson 37: Detecting a Regime Change](/education/curriculum/intermediate/37-detecting-a-regime-change.html)
• [Lesson 38: What a Timeframe Is](/education/curriculum/intermediate/38-what-a-timeframe-is.html)
• [Lesson 44: Volatility as a Quantity](/education/curriculum/intermediate/44-volatility-as-a-quantity.html)

**The cost of waiting:** lesson 37 prices what each bar of confirmation buys and costs.
kb.indicators:
**Indicators, Honestly:**

An indicator is a function of numbers you already have, and four consequences follow from that sentence alone.

**What the course measures:**
• It cannot add information: anything readable off the line was readable off the prices
• It discards, and the discarding can be counted
• It is late by an amount you compute rather than guess — 4.50 bars for a ten-period simple average
• Two standard RSI implementations print thirteen readings above 70 and none on the same sixty closes

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 48: What an Indicator Is](/education/curriculum/intermediate/48-what-an-indicator-is.html)
• [Lesson 49: Repainting](/education/curriculum/intermediate/49-repainting.html)
• [Lesson 50: Moving Averages as Support](/education/curriculum/intermediate/50-moving-averages.html)
• [Lesson 51: Oscillators Under Regime](/education/curriculum/intermediate/51-oscillators-under-regime.html)
• [Lesson 52: Confirmation Bias, Measured](/education/curriculum/intermediate/52-confirmation-bias.html)

**The measured version of confirmation:** twelve indicator configurations are 1.71 independent opinions.
kb.backtest:
**Backtesting as Evidence:**

Running a rule over past prices to see what it would have done, treated as evidence with a strength you can state rather than as a result.

**What the course measures:**
• A search of 253 rules turns up a winner at 9.84 a share against 5.68 for holding, on 7 trades, t = 3.65
• Because 253 settings were searched, the bar it must clear is 3.54 rather than 1.65
• Judging continuously instead of at a fixed horizon takes a dead system’s pass rate from 5.05 per cent to 24.25
• Walk-forward removes one way of fooling yourself and not the others

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 62: What Would Have to Happen](/education/curriculum/advanced/62-from-observation-to-hypothesis.html)
• [Lesson 63: Backtesting as Evidence](/education/curriculum/advanced/63-backtesting.html)
• [Lesson 64: The Price of Looking](/education/curriculum/advanced/64-overfitting.html)
• [Lesson 65: The Horizon You Fix First](/education/curriculum/advanced/65-forward-testing-and-deployment.html)

**The four subtractions** between a gross figure and one worth believing are in lesson 63.
kb.overfitting:
**Overfitting and the Price of Looking:**

Choosing a rule’s settings on the same data used to judge it, so the judgement measures the search rather than the rule.

**What the course measures:**
• A search of 15,000 configurations over 156 trades manufactures 0.317 of an R before the market does anything
• That figure comes out of the two counts alone, with no prices in it
• The bar rises with the search: 3.54 rather than 1.65 after 253 settings
• At one live candidate in ten, two ordinary habits take a disciplined test from 43.2 per cent real to 6.0

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 64: The Price of Looking](/education/curriculum/advanced/64-overfitting.html)
• [Lesson 63: Backtesting as Evidence](/education/curriculum/advanced/63-backtesting.html)
• [Lesson 84: The Share That Is Real](/education/curriculum/professional/84-behavioural-finance.html)

**The defence:** state the horizon and the search size before you look.
kb.portfolio:
**Portfolio and Correlation:**

How many independent bets a set of positions actually amounts to, and which of your limits binds before the others.

**What the course measures:**
• Two rules on one instrument at the measured correlation carry 1.03 bets rather than two
• However many you add, the total tops out at 1.06
• Twenty positions at an average pairwise 0.3 carry the risk of three independent ones
• The daily-loss limit is the only column that can be enforced before an order is sent

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 71: How Many Bets You Are Carrying](/education/curriculum/professional/71-positions-are-one-position.html)
• [Lesson 72: The Day Every Stop Hits](/education/curriculum/professional/72-portfolio-heat.html)
• [Lesson 73: The Weights You Can Hold](/education/curriculum/professional/73-allocating-across-strategies.html)
• [Lesson 74: The Window Decides](/education/curriculum/professional/74-where-portfolio-theory-fails.html)
• [Lesson 75: Which Limit Binds First](/education/curriculum/professional/75-institutional-risk-controls.html)

**The finding:** correlation moves enough between two halves of one record to change the answer.
kb.book:
**A Book of Rules:**

What a whole grid of rules earns against its best member, where the result came from, and whether every member earns its place.

**What the course measures:**
• The equal-weight book of 253 rules earns 4.16 a share, exactly the average of the rules inside it
• Three of the book’s twenty-eight moves carry 80.5 per cent of its return
• Turnover takes 4.10 to 3.70 and inverts the ranking inside the book
• Three of four leave-one-out deletions improve the book

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 91: What the Whole Grid Earns](/education/curriculum/professional/91-what-the-whole-grid-earns.html)
• [Lesson 92: Where the Result Came From](/education/curriculum/professional/92-where-the-result-came-from.html)
• [Lesson 93: The Rule That Trades the Most](/education/curriculum/professional/93-the-rule-that-trades-the-most.html)
• [Lesson 94: The Ride You Actually Bought](/education/curriculum/professional/94-the-ride-you-actually-bought.html)
• [Lesson 95: The Book on One Card](/education/curriculum/professional/95-the-book-on-one-card.html)

**The test:** delete each member in turn and recompute every column, not just the return.
kb.business:
**Trading as a Business:**

What the pace, the cost, the withdrawal and the record do to each other once a person is living on the result.

**What the course measures:**
• 13 orders in 28 days is 4.875 completed trades a month
• A genuine tenth-of-an-R edge still loses 41.3 per cent of its months
• A 500 withdrawal against 487.50 earned needs a balance of 102,564 to break even
• Five rows fail in a fixed order, and the business fails at the second: the cost

**Lessons:**

kb.psychology:
**The Trader, Measured:**

Four habits priced on the same seven trades, so the argument is about arithmetic rather than about discipline.

**What the course measures:**
• Taking the profit at the first green close costs 2.20 a share and leaves the win rate exactly where it was
• A quarter-R stop costs 5.90 a share
• Adding those predicts 1.74 left; running both at once leaves 4.44
• 26.7 per cent of everything that ever showed on screen was given back

**Lessons:**
• [Lesson 86: Taking the Profit](/education/curriculum/professional/86-taking-the-profit.html)
• [Lesson 87: The Second Exit](/education/curriculum/professional/87-the-second-exit.html)
• [Lesson 88: The Size of the Next One](/education/curriculum/professional/88-the-size-of-the-next-one.html)
• [Lesson 89: The Money That Was Showing](/education/curriculum/professional/89-the-money-that-was-showing.html)
• [Lesson 90: The Four Habits Together](/education/curriculum/professional/90-the-four-habits-together.html)

**Why the addition fails:** two exits do not stack, they compete, and only the earlier one ever fires.
